description: A dedicated health monitoring system designed for astronauts on active space missions.
summary:
AstroCare is a web-based health monitoring app for astronauts that works offline and warns early when something goes wrong.

What we developed: Astronauts log measurements, symptoms, exercise, food and medication. Their home screen shows one clear status (Normal, Caution or Critical) with charts of all health areas and recent alerts. Every reading is compared with reference thresholds and with the astronaut’s own baseline. The health team gets a live chart or the last data received if the ground link drops, next to the reference values.

How it addresses the challenge: It turns daily health data into clear alerts. For example, a stress level of 5 raises a Critical alarm with sound. If nobody acknowledges an alarm in time, it escalates to a backup health officer and then to mission management, so no alarm is lost. Roles, offline use, glove mode, night mode and unit options are built for space conditions.

Why it matters: Far from Earth, small health changes can become serious. AstroCare helps crews and ground teams notice them sooner. The CO₂ and radiation limits follow NASA-STD-3001, and the other thresholds are demo values that need clinical validation.
details:
AstroCare: Astronaut Health Monitoring and Alert System

AstroCare is a health tracking app for astronauts living and working in space. It records daily health data, compares it with reference values, warns when something goes wrong, and makes sure no alarm is lost.

For the astronaut

  • The Home screen shows one overall status: Normal, Caution or Critical.
  • A donut chart shows how many health areas are normal, in caution or critical, and a bar chart shows the alerts of the last 7 days.
  • Health areas are sorted so the most critical ones appear first.
  • The Track screen has five tabs: Measurements, Symptoms, Exercise, Food and Medication. Each tab has its own chart, for example a trend line with reference thresholds, symptom severity, exercise minutes per day, and nutrition against daily targets.
  • Reminders show the time left or overdue time, and there is no snooze.
  • Other tools include an illness and treatment log, a summary and flight surgeon report, a user guide and a personal profile.

Alerts

  • Every reading is compared with reference thresholds and with the astronaut’s own pre-flight baseline.
  • Stress is rated from 1 to 5. A value of 4 raises a Caution alert and a value of 5 (high) raises a Critical alarm with sound.
  • Several areas getting worse at the same time create a combined risk alert.
  • Missing data also creates an alert.

For the health team

  • Health team members see the alarms of the crew and acknowledge them.
  • A Live screen shows a chart of any measurement, updated automatically, or the last data received if the ground link is lost.
  • A table lists the latest value of each measurement next to its reference values and status.
  • An alarm that is not acknowledged in time moves to a backup health officer and then to mission management.
  • Roles: astronaut (own data only), health team, backup health officer, mission management, and a read-only manager console.

Built for space conditions

  • Works offline and sends records when the ground link returns.
  • UTC and mission elapsed time, metric and US customary units.
  • Glove mode with large touch targets, and a red low-blue-light night mode.
  • Destination setting for the ISS, the Moon or Mars.
  • Reference values: the CO₂ limit (3 mmHg) and the career radiation limit (600 mSv) follow NASA-STD-3001. Other thresholds are demo values, marked as unverified in the app.

Test panel for reviewers
A side panel lets reviewers sign in as any role without a PIN, send stress levels 1 to 5, run scenarios such as sleep loss, fluid shift, radiation event and cabin CO₂ issue, send any reading, and reset the demo data.
